newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends weaker and at lows, mixed selling.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends weaker and at lows, mixed selling.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures ended sharply weaker and near the day's lows amid mixed selling and a dearth of buying, market sources said.
The negative sentiment was prompted by the U.S. Department of Agriculture's export and sales report, which put new sales for the week ended April 24 at 56,500 480-lb bales in the 1996/97 crop.
"The market had been holding anemically for three days and couldn't get a rally going," a dealer said. "The specs then the trade started selling and away we went."
The most-active July contract ended 1.34 cents weaker at 72.31 cents per lb, having ranged from 73.20 to 72.20 cents. New-crop December finished 0.89 cent weaker at 75.05 cents.
Volume was estimated at 10,000 lots compared with Wednesday's official 4,868 lots.
Support had been pegged at 73.00 cents basis the July contract and is now seen at key 70.05 cents, the contract's lifetime low.
